# Terrain loading fix and mobile controls

This development preview supersedes `dev-2026.10.08` for browser play. It is built
from `89c5aa394d27e64b41a8ac4fc880ddf1144e0ecc` in PR #6.

## Fixes

- Terrain output now streams during generation. CPU time spent generating a
  view no longer counts as a stalled network connection before sending starts.
  This fixes a reproduced timeout that affects slow servers, including RISC-V
  hardware. Peers that actually stop reading still have bounded queues/timeouts.
- The browser enters when the spawn position and its chunk are available; it
  no longer waits for the server's redundant final teleport. Loading progress
  and inactivity errors are visible.
- Buffered input drains safely after expensive generation. Mesh building yields
  between layers to keep input responsive on slower mobile CPUs.

## Mobile play

Touch controls activate automatically on touch-capable devices; a checkbox on
the join screen can override this. Drag the left stick to move, drag the world
to look, hold **Mine** or **Jump**, and tap **Use** to place/use a selected item.
Movement, looking and jumping support simultaneous fingers. Use the **Inventory**,
**Chat**, **Drop** and **Respawn** buttons, and tap/scroll the hotbar to choose a
slot. Inventory has a **Split stack / place one item** option. Portrait and
landscape layouts are supported. WebGL remains required.

## Download and update

| File | CPU | HTML5 client |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `lapis-obsidian-alpine-riscv64-web.tar.gz` | RISC-V 64-bit | Enabled |
| `lapis-obsidian-alpine-amd64-web.tar.gz` | AMD64 / x86-64 | Enabled |
| `lapis-obsidian-alpine-riscv64-native.tar.gz` | RISC-V 64-bit | Disabled |
| `lapis-obsidian-alpine-amd64-native.tar.gz` | AMD64 / x86-64 | Disabled |

Stop the server, extract the matching package, and replace the executable.
Restart it from your existing world directory, then reload the page in your
browser. Existing configuration and world files can be retained. For web play,
choose a **web** package and open `http://<server-address>:8080/` (or your configured
web port). Settings remain:

```ini
port=25565
web-address=0.0.0.0
web-port=8080
```

The packages contain static Linux/musl binaries, documentation and license
notices. `source.tar.gz` is the matching source; per-variant `.buildinfo.txt`
files and `SHA256SUMS` record the build and download checksums. Source builds
still require `LAPIS_OBSIDIAN_WEB_CLIENT=1` to enable the client.

## Validation and remaining scope

The [source build](https://github.com/aksulightning/lapisobsidian/actions/runs/37762050353)
runs full normal/sanitized regressions, transport timeout/input-buffer tests,
and gameplay integration on AMD64 and RISC-V under QEMU: login, 25 chunks, two
players, inventory, mining/placement, movement and reconnect. Chromium tests
cover actual terrain pixels, login without the redundant teleport, desktop
controls and mobile multitouch/cancellation, mining/placement, chat, inventory,
and portrait/landscape layouts.

RISC-V hardware performance and individual physical phones remain unverified;
mobile tests use Chromium device emulation. This remains an experimental client
with flat-color blocks/simple entities and simplified mining/collision. Flight,
skins, sound, particles and sign editing are not included. Existing offline
identity, permissions and unencrypted HTTP/WebSocket behavior remain in effect;
see the included guide for TLS proxy setup.
